sentences.text: The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 04-02-2022 at about 4.30 p.m., the petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-59-H-7935.

When he reached near Total LPG Gas Bunk, Bommasandra,
on Bengaluru-Hosur NH-44 service road.

At that time, one Tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709, driven by its driver with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came from opposite side and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Oxford Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an in- patient.
Earlier to the accident he was working as Security Guard and was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Hebbagodi Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Tempo traveler for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted that, it is the owner of the vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709 and the same is insured with the respondent No.2.
Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1 is the company and the vehicle is registered in the name of company.
The same was driven by its driver, who has not been made party in the proceedings.

Further it is contended that, when its vehicle reached Bommasandra at Bengaluru-Hosur NH-44, the rider of the two-wheeler vehicle/petitioner all of a sudden came with high speed, in a zig zag movement and dashed to the Tempo traveler.
Due to high speed the rider lost control over his vehicle and suddenly came to wrong side and dashed against the Tempo traveler.
The Tempo traveler driver applied the brake and avoided further damage towards the petitioner.

Further it is contended that, its driver himself admitted the petitioner to hospital and paid the first aid charges bill and paid the miscellaneous charges and he has spent more than Rs.10,000/- for petitioner's treatment on humanitarian ground.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the petitioner was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the two- wheeler at the time of accident.
Further it has contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, the LR's of deceased respondent No.1 i.e. respondent No.1(a) to (c) in their written statement have denied all the allegations made in the petition.

They have contended that, the respondent No.1 is the company represented by Neeta Adappa, Anusha Adappa and Siddharth Puttupogula Sarveswara Rao vs When It Strikes Crisis Management Pvt Td on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166128318/

sentences.text: 3 Adappa, the respondent No.1 is employee i.e. driver was driving a Tempo traveler bearing Reg.
No.KA-51-C- 7709 at the time of accident, the Tempo traveler driver had been an employee of the respondent No.1's company for a period of two years and he was holding valid driving licence.
The respondent No.2 has been given the duty of pick up and drop of the employees of the respondent No.1 company.
Further it is contended that, on 04-02-2022 the employee of the respondent No.1 was carrying various other employees from the company office back to their homes.

At about 4.30 p.m., when the petitioner was riding a scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-59-H-7935, he was aware of the fact that the Tempo traveler was approaching from the opposite direction, as there was no divider in the road.
The tempo was clearly within the confines of the road.

Inspite of having knowledge of the Tempo traveler, the petitioner hurriedly and negligently at a high speed tried crossing/moving his vehicle across the road to another side of the road without any precaution and he was riding the said scooter without helmet.

Further it is contended that, due to the rash actions of the petitioner, who had hurriedly and negligently tried crossing/moving his vehicle across the road and the respondent No.1's employee having witnessed this negligent act of the petitioner, suddenly applied the brakes of his vehicle, in order to avoid collision.
Inspite of applying the brakes, the Tempo traveler collided with the petitioner's scooter and the petitioner fell off his vehicle and suffered injuries on his head.
The respondent No.1's employee has taken all the reasonable steps to secure medical attention for the injured person, by conveying the petitioner to the nearest hospital i.e. Oxford Hospital.
It has denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
It has contended that, the Tempo traveler was insured with respondent No.2 vide policy No.3003/231303038/00/000, valid from 08-11-2011 to 07-11- 2022, which was valid as on the date of accident.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
6. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Section 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has denied that, the alleged accident was caused due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709.

On the contrary the alleged accident has occurred only due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 59-H-7935, who without observing the traffic suddenly rushed his vehicle and he himself dashed against the tempo which resulted in the alleged accident.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle drove the same without having valid and effective driving licence.
The owner of the Tempo traveler willfully entrusted the tempo traveler knowing fully well that, his driver was not having valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.

Further the said tempo traveler was not having valid permit and fitness certificate to ply the same in the public road and hence the same is in contravention of the policy conditions and also the Motor Vehicle Act.
Hence, it is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.
Further, it has sought permission to contest the matter on all the grounds available under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.3003/231303038/00/000 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.Ka-51-C-7709 and it was valid from 08-11-2011 to 07-11-2022.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 6, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709 and dashing the same to the oncoming motorcycle of the petitioner.
Further it reveals that, in the said accident the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries on his head, left leg, liver and other parts of the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.6, has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.

14. At the outset, is it pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
the involvement of offending Tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709 in the said accident,
issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

The respondents have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and they have taken specific defence that, the said accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/ rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-59-H- 7935, as the petitioner all of a sudden rode his motrocycle with high speed, in a zig zag manner and due to high speed he lost control over his vehicle, suddenly came to wrong side and dashed against the Tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative/Legal Manager of respondent No.2 insurance company, there is absolutely no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondents, to establish the above contentions.

If really the accident has taken place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-09-H- 7935 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending Tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709, the same could have been easily established by the respondents by examining the eye-witness to the alleged accident.
But, the respondents have not taken any strain to examine the eye-witness to the alleged accident, for the reasons best known to them.

In such circumstances, there is absolutely no evidence on record to show that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-09-H-7935 and the petitioner himself has dashed to the offending Tempo traveler.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Tempo traveler and dashing the same to an oncoming motorcycle of the petitioner.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates Puttupogula Sarveswara Rao vs When It Strikes Crisis Management Pvt Td on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166128318/

Further, the Ex.P.3 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 25 feet wide Bengaluru-Hosur NH-44 Service road, near Bommasandra Total LPG Gas Bunk, Attibele Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru, in between the offending tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709 and the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-09-H-7935 of the petitioner.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.4, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the offending vehicle and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle of the petitioner, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondents have not produced any rebuttal evidence to show that, the said documents are false and concocted documents.

There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.6 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending tempo traveler bearing Reg. No. KA-51-C-7709 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report filed by the investigation officer and other police records,
regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident,
negligence of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
16.

Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.5 wound certificate, Ex.P.7 discharge summary,
Ex.P.13 case- sheet, Ex.P.14 clinical notes, Ex.P.16 neuro-psychological assessment report with work sheet, Ex.P.17 MRI brain report, Ex.P.18 MRI scan films (total 4), Ex.P.20 case-sheet, Ex.P.22 out-patient record with examination report and Ex.P.23 X-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in a road traffic accident.

The P.W.3 and P.W.4, who are the doctors who have examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, have clearly deposed in their evidence that, the petitioner has sustained injuries i.e. head injury with left occipital bone fracture, right tibia shaft fracture and liver laceration in a road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 and P.W.4 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from their mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no rebuttal evidence placed on record by the respondents to show that, the above medical records produced by the petitioner are false documents.
17. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) 11 SCC Puttupogula Sarveswara Rao vs When It Strikes Crisis Management Pvt Td on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166128318/
7 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
18.

No.KA-51-C-7709.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:

While answering the above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the petitioner has successfully proved that, the accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tempo traveler bearing Reg. No.KA-51-C-7709 and he has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
As per the medical records placed on record by the petitioner, he has sustained head injury with left occipital bone fracture, right tibia shaft fracture and liver laceration.
Therefore, this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life,
loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
i) Towards loss of future income: In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9, the date of birth of the petitioner is 14-03-1994.
The accident has taken place on 04-02-2022 at about 4:30 p.m.
This clearly goes show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 28 years.

Further, the P.W.3, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered head injury and for the said injury the petitioner has taken conservative treatment.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered permanent neurological disability of 66%, due to head injury.

sentences.text: Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.3 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.3 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 04-02-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 21-08-2023, which is after lapse of one year and six months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, he has clearly admitted in his cross-examination that, the petitioner has not undergone any surgery, the treatment of the petitioner is completed and he does not require any further treatment.

Further he has stated that, the petitioner can follow the command and identify the persons with great difficulties, the communication, selfcare and other inter-personal activities of the petitioner are not normal.

Likewise, the P.W.4, who is the doctor, who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered head injury + chest injury +
abdominal injury and right tibia shaft fracture and for the said injuries the petitioner has taken conservative treatment.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries suffered by the petitioner he found that, the petitioner has suffered 38% disability to the right lower limb and 19% disability to the whole body.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.4 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
Further, he has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

But, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.4 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 04-02-2022 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 24-05-2024,
which is after lapse of two years and three months from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, P.W.4 has clearly admitted in his cross- examination that, the fracture sustained to the petitioner is united, the petitioner has undergone complete treatment, the leg fracture of the petitioner is treated conservatively.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.4 while arriving the disability to the whole body of the petitioner he has considered half of the disability to right lower limb and came to conclusion that, the petitioner has suffered 19% disability to the whole body.

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment, oral and documentary evidence available on record and the present Neuro-Psychological status of the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the disability of 40% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 40% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
